questions.prompt: The wise king was advising the citizens to fear the coming war.
questions.answer: Rēx sapiēns cīvēs monēbat ut bellum ventūrum timērent.

questions.prompt: We shall hold the city with a strong garrison, though the enemy threatens.
questions.answer: Urbem validō praesidiō tenēbimus, quamquam hostis imminet.

questions.prompt: The general ordered the soldiers to remain within the camp.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitēs intrā castra manēre iussit.

questions.prompt: If you had warned me sooner, I would not have feared the danger.
questions.answer: Sī mē mātūrius monuissēs, perīculum nōn timuissem.

questions.prompt: The teacher instructs the boys with great authority.
questions.answer: Magister puerōs magnā auctōritāte docet.

questions.prompt: Let us advise the young men, lest they destroy their own reputation.
questions.answer: Iuvenēs moneāmus, nē fāmam suam dēleant.

questions.prompt: The mother feared for her son, who was lingering in the woods.
questions.answer: Māter fīliō timēbat, quī in silvīs manēbat.

questions.prompt: The philosopher used to warn his disciples about empty pleasures.
questions.answer: Philosophus discipulōs dē vānīs voluptātibus monēbat.

questions.prompt: The frightened people were moving their goods out of the burning city.
questions.answer: Populus territus bona ex urbe ārdente movēbat.

questions.prompt: We ought to obey the laws which our ancestors established.
questions.answer: Lēgibus pārēre dēbēmus quās maiōrēs statuērunt.

questions.prompt: The consul warned that the treaty would not remain unbroken.
questions.answer: Cōnsul monuit foedus nōn integrum mānsūrum esse.

questions.prompt: The old man advises his grandson to shun the crowd's empty flattery.
questions.answer: Senex nepōtem monet ut inānem turbae adūlātiōnem vītet.

questions.prompt: Though wounded, the soldier held his ground and terrified the enemy.
questions.answer: Mīles vulnerātus locum tenēbat et hostēs terrēbat.

questions.prompt: May the gods increase our strength and destroy the tyrant's pride.
questions.answer: Deī vīrēs nostrās augeant et superbiam tyrannī dēleant.

questions.prompt: I shall advise you as a friend, whatever you may decide.
questions.answer: Tē ut amīcus monēbō, quidquid cēnseās.

questions.prompt: The queen was holding the scepter which her father had left behind.
questions.answer: Rēgīna sceptrum tenēbat quod pater relīquerat.

questions.prompt: Warn the guards to keep silent, lest they betray our plan.
questions.answer: Custōdēs monē ut taceant, nē cōnsilium nostrum prōdant.

questions.prompt: The physician warned the sick man that he should not fear death.
questions.answer: Medicus aegrōtum monuit nē mortem timēret.

questions.prompt: We were sitting in the shade while the poet recited his verses.
questions.answer: In umbrā sedēbāmus dum poēta versūs suōs recitābat.

questions.prompt: Having been warned by the omen, the leader remained in his tent.
questions.answer: Ōmine monitus dux in tabernāculō mānsit.

questions.prompt: The angry master used to frighten the slaves with harsh threats.
questions.answer: Dominus īrātus servōs dūrīs minīs terrēbat.

questions.prompt: Let him beware of the flatterer, who advises only for his own gain.
questions.answer: Caveat adūlātōrem, quī sōlum suā causā monet.
